item.title: The case for BCacheFS inclusion in PVE
item.author: invalid@example.com (alexskysilk)
item.dc:creator: alexskysilk
item.content:encoded:
PVE has (and continues to have) a large presence in the homelab/self hosting crowd. The Primary filesystem option employed for single host applications was and is ZFS, due to its robust featureset and code maturity. Yet ZFS's core structural geometry—fixed virtual device (vdev) layouts, rigid pool topologies, and bolt-on workarounds like RAIDZ expansion or special vdevs—shows strain when modern single-node servers mix NVMe, SATA SSDs, and high-capacity hard drives.
